cards.title: Per-MIC PTA Definition and Calculation Basis
cards.claim: Probability of Target Attainment (PTA) is the probability that at least a specific value of a PK/PD target (PDT) is achieved at a certain MIC. It is calculated by simulating individual exposures (e.g., via Monte Carlo) and determining the proportion of simulated individuals whose exposure index (e.g., fAUC/MIC or %fT>MIC) meets or exceeds the target value for that specific MIC.
conditions: Requires a qualified PK model with explicit parameter/distribution assumptions.
Requires a qualified PD target with defined endpoint, index basis (free/total), and time window.
Applicable when prospective probability of target attainment is needed for specified regimens and susceptibility values.
Must separate uncertainty in parameter estimates from variability between individuals.
required_inputs: Qualified PK scenario with explicit parameter/distribution assumptions.
Qualified PD target with endpoint, index basis, and window.
Explicit human-variability assumptions if human observations are unavailable.
limitations: PTA is not probability of clinical cure.
Does not establish observed human inter-individual variability (IIV) from animal IIV or parameter standard errors.
Cannot validate human PK/PD in the absence of independent human observations.
Abstract-only or partial excerpts do not support full methodological validation.
cards.downstream_use: Use to determine if a specific dosing regimen achieves a predefined microbiological target for a given MIC, informing dose selection or breakpoint determination.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Per-MIC PTA definition: exposure distribution, target, basis and window
